cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's accounting machine compare October's results to budget for HANGS Construction.
First it reads the closed books by department, and the budget the board approved.
Next it compares every department to its budget.
October came in about $168,000 below budget.
Then it resizes the budget to the work actually done.
Now it drills into the biggest variances, line by line in the ledger.
It tests each manager's explanation against what the ledger shows.
Most of the shortfall is one job whose costs ran far over plan.
A $16,800 software plan for next year was expensed all at once in October.
Then it reforecasts the rest of the year on signed work only.
An unsigned $640,000 job is shown as possible upside, not counted.
The full year now looks like a loss of about $154,000, against a budgeted profit.
All done. The board pack is drafted, with commentary on every large variance and four items to settle first. Nothing was posted or sent; the CFO reviews and signs.
Jumping to the results. A person still reviews every item before anything is posted, paid or sent.
